claims.text: Substrate-induced interfacial strain and nanoscale size effects alter magneto-structural coupling in as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films and nanoribbons.
Altered magneto-structural coupling affects magnetic-domain nucleation and pinning.
Changes in domain nucleation and pinning shift or suppress the magnetocaloric response.
Changes in domain nucleation and pinning enhance hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Limited heat-transfer rates prevent complete latent-heat exchange at increased cycling frequencies.
A compliant buffer layer or reduced film-substrate adhesion will reduce substrate-induced strain without changing the alloy's intrinsic phases.
Changing the interfacial strain field modifies lattice parameters.
Changing the interfacial strain field modifies local interfacial energy barriers.
Strain-induced changes in lattice parameters and local energy barriers influence magnetic-domain configurations and nucleation dynamics.
Reducing substrate-induced strain lessens excessive magnetic-domain pinning.
Reducing substrate-induced strain shifts the energy landscape of the magneto-structural transition.
Reduced pinning and a shifted transition-energy landscape make the phase change more reversible.
A compliant-buffer sample will exhibit a larger isothermal entropy change than the rigid-substrate control.
A compliant-buffer sample will exhibit a sharper, more bulk-like magnetocaloric transition than the rigid-substrate control.
A compliant-buffer sample will exhibit a narrower hysteresis loop than the rigid-substrate control under low-field cycling.
Rigid-substrate baseline samples have strong substrate-induced strain that causes a muted or shifted magnetocaloric response and pronounced hysteresis.
The proposed mechanism is applicable below 100 mT and near the magneto-structural transition temperature.
Heat-transfer limitations continue to cap effective cycle frequency even after strain is reduced.
